content:
You can name a Prayer Leader and still go a month without gathering to pray. You can also watch the planter's household cover meals, rides, and late setup because no one else was asked. Those are different problems. They need different people.

This guide is how you arrange both. The Core Group owns prayer. The Prayer Leader coordinates a prayer team. A separate care team handles practical help the planter asks for. The care team does not counsel. Neither team sees private check-ins or family disclosures unless the planter has chosen a specific line to share. Everyfield does not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health, and it does not certify either team.

---

## Two teams, two jobs

Keep the work on two lists. The prayer team intercedes. The care team carries practical loads. If one group does both, the person who drops off dinner also hears a story, and that story can land on a prayer email the planter never approved.

### Prayer team

Named requests, gatherings, and Sunday prayer. The Prayer Leader leads it. It sees only what the planter shares for prayer.

### Care team

Meals, rides, childcare, and setup help. A different coordinator leads it. It sees only the practical ask.

Prayer is one of the [8 Critical Success Factors](/wiki/frameworks/8-critical-success-factors-overview). The factor is a praying Core Group, not a Prayer Leader title. Recruiting, training, and Sunday prayer sit in [The Prayer Leader Role](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/prayer-leader-role). The launch roles are listed in [Key Leadership Roles Overview](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/key-leadership-roles-overview). This article is about the team around that role, and the practical team beside it.

<Callout type="warning">
A meal rota is not pastoral care. The person who brings dinner is not the planter's counselor. If the talk turns to a marriage, to mental health, or to whether the planter should continue, stop. Point them to a pastor they name, or to a professional they choose.
</Callout>

---

## Keep a rhythm, not only a title

A filled role is not a praying Core Group. Prayer belongs to every member, the way inviting and giving do. The Prayer Leader coordinates. The people still have to show up.

Write down the rhythm you mean to keep:

- The day and length of the gathering where you pray together
- How prayer sits inside leadership meetings, past a one-line close
- Who will say something if that gathering did not happen in the last month

Bring a missed month to the leadership meeting. Ask what got in the way, and put the next date on the calendar before you leave. Do not treat the gap, or the title, as a verdict on anyone's faith. No tool should score calling, character, or spiritual health from a prayer roster.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving;"* — Colossians 4:2 (LSB)
</Callout>

---

## What the prayer team carries

Ask the Prayer Leader to recruit people who will pray, then train them. Training covers how to pray with a person after a service, and how to keep a confidence. The role article already names a Sunday prayer team, prayer partners, and intercessors. Do not build a second system beside that one.

Send requests in the planter's words. If they did not ask you to share it, it is not on the list. A useful request is specific enough to pray and plain enough to forward. A venue decision, guests for Launch Sunday, strength for the preaching, and protection for the household can be prayed in public. The detail that belongs in a private conversation stays off the email.

The Prayer Leader keeps those requests in front of the body, usually in a short email, and plans the corporate gatherings. A long, vague meeting trains people to skip the next one. A clear hour, with a few named requests, is a rhythm you can keep.

<Callout type="tip">
Read the request back to the planter before you send it. If they would not say that sentence in the Core Group, rewrite it or drop it.
</Callout>

---

## What stays off both lists

A private check-in stays with the person who wrote it. Do not copy it into a prayer email, a care thread, or a shared note. Serving on either team does not open that door. A network office does not get a copy because someone on the team thought it would help.

A full launch calendar does not tell you the planter is well. Launch progress and the planter's own life are different questions. The second one belongs with a pastor the planter names, or with a life mentor who is investing in them as a person. [Finding a Coach/Mentor](/wiki/discovery/finding-a-coach-mentor) describes that relationship. It is not a slot on the care rota.

Do not ask a tool to write the prayers, or to tell you whether the planter is fit to continue. Those are human conversations.

<Callout type="important">
If a volunteer hears something the planter did not ask them to share, they leave it off both lists. They ask the planter what, if anything, may be passed on. If someone may be in immediate danger, they contact a pastor the planter trusts and local emergency services. They do not post it.
</Callout>

---

## Practical help, and the line it does not cross

The care team is a small group for practical help the planter has requested. Agree on the members with the planter. Name a coordinator who is not the Prayer Leader, so the two lists do not live in the same notebook.

The team may bring meals on weeks the planter names. It may provide childcare during a meeting, under the household's own rules. It may give a ride, help with a move, or help set up a venue. It may cover one stated errand, then stop.

It does not counsel, diagnose, or advise a marriage. It does not decide whether the planter is called, fit, or spiritually healthy. It does not interview the family, and it does not keep notes on the home. It does not pass household details to the prayer team so people can pray.

When a need is more than an errand, the coordinator tells a pastor the planter names, or encourages the planter to choose a professional. Do not build a file. A name and a date are enough.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ."* — Galatians 6:2 (LSB)
</Callout>

For this team, the burden is the practical load the planter asked you to carry. The verse is not a reason to pry.

---

## How the two coordinators stay in touch

The Prayer Leader and the care coordinator need a short check. Compare dates. Name the public prayer requests. Name the practical gaps the planter already approved. Do not review how the planter seems.

Meet once a month, and sooner when a request has a date on it. The planter approves any line that names their household before it goes to either team.

If only one person is willing to lead both, do not merge the teams. Ask that person to keep two lists and two messages, and ask for a second name as soon as someone is willing. An empty care role is better than a prayer email full of private news.

---

## Mistakes that tangle the two teams

- You appoint a Prayer Leader and call the prayer factor done.
- One team both prays and checks on the family.
- A family strain goes on the church-wide prayer note.
- Care volunteers sit in on coach conversations or private check-ins.
- A tool, or a launch checklist, is asked to say whether the planter is doing well.
- Either team is used to decide who may serve or who may launch.

---

## The weeks before Launch Sunday

The last month already has a prayer pattern: one day a week of fasting, a gathering with worship and prayer, and a shared meal, with the Senior Pastor leading. Follow [Launch Team Spiritual Preparation](/wiki/pre-launch/launch-team-spiritual-preparation) for that rhythm, for prayer coverage on Launch Sunday, and for rest. Outside partners get the same public requests as the prayer team, not a private briefing. Do not rebuild that pattern here.

Add one care-team question for those weeks. What practical help does the household want, and what should people stop offering? Write the answer down. Then leave them alone on the evening you promised. Help that will not stop is not care.

Walk this list with the planter before you call either team ready:

- [ ] The Core Group has a written prayer time, and someone notices if a month passes without it
- [ ] Prayer requests go out only in the planter's words
- [ ] Prayer partners know to keep a confidence
- [ ] The care coordinator is not the Prayer Leader
- [ ] Care is practical help only, with a named pastor or professional for anything further
- [ ] Neither team can open private check-ins
- [ ] The planter has approved every line that names their household

The care responsibilities and the limits of volunteer support in this article are a model draft awaiting human authorship by Sebastian (or a pastor he names) before approval. Sebastian reviews every article and acts as that human author. This draft is not approved pastoral-care guidance.

Wording calls: title kept as Prayer Team and Care Team, with care defined as practical help only. The care coordinator is a different person from the Prayer Leader. Referral is to a pastor the planter names or a professional the planter chooses, because the planter is often the Senior Pastor. Sort order is 12, after The Prayer Leader Role. "Last month" is the church's own notice, not a product attestation window. If a volunteer believes someone may be in immediate danger, they contact a pastor the planter trusts and local emergency services, and they do not post the disclosure. This article does not draft or close C1, Caring for the Planter and Family. Gender-neutral they for the planter. Galatians 6:2 is applied only to the practical load the planter requested. Colossians 4:2 is quoted without a gloss.

The body does not name Everyfield attestation fields, private-check-in questions, or Evry. The limits are written to stay consistent with REQ-PI-015, REQ-PI-038, REQ-EVR-001, and Bryan's C05, C19, C20, and C21.
